sections.h2: How fast can I sell a house in Vancouver, WA?
sections.html:
How quickly a Vancouver sale closes comes down to the buyer's money, the title work and one county stop that every Clark County deed must make. Cash removes the lender from the picture, so owners facing a move, an inherited house or a big repair bill often start there. Listing the traditional way means showings, an appraisal and a loan approval first.

Vancouver is the Clark County seat, sitting on the Columbia River's north bank opposite Portland. About 199,698 people live here, 4.6 percent more than in 2020. That growth brings plenty of buyers and investors to the same streets you live on, so collecting more than one offer is realistic.

Owners occupy 50.8 percent of homes, so roughly half the housing stock is rented. Landlords and investors may bid on a fixer-upper just as readily as a household planning to live there.

Downtown and most of the older housing sit in West Vancouver. The east side grew after an annexation in 1997 that brought in 11,258 acres and 58,171 residents, with NE Andresen Road as the usual boundary between the halves.

Several well-known neighborhoods began as wartime housing. When the Kaiser shipyard drew tens of thousands of workers in the 1940s, the Vancouver Housing Authority was created along with six developments: Fruit Valley, Fourth Plain Village, Bagley Downs, Ogden Meadows, Burton Homes and McLoughlin Heights. Expect inspectors in those areas to press on age-related items.

  • Original wiring and panels
  • Galvanized or older supply plumbing
  • Foundations, crawl spaces and drainage
  • Roofs and insulation

Roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take the most wear from about 42 inches of rain a year, falling mostly from fall to spring, so look at them before you price the house.

Over a third of the urban area is in unincorporated pockets, among them Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek. Confirm your address is within city limits, because the permit and rental rules that follow apply only inside them.

Vancouver Public Schools serves most of the west side and Evergreen Public Schools most of the east. A few edges of the city belong to Camas or Battle Ground, so look up your street with the district before quoting schools to a buyer.

Interstates 5 and 205 both cross the Columbia into Portland, SR 14 runs east from downtown, and SR 500 links I-5 to I-205. Rush-hour traffic is heavy on the Interstate Bridge and the Glenn Jackson Bridge, and C-Tran runs local and express buses. Homes near the freeways often appeal to commuters who value a shorter trip.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit before selling a Vancouver house?
sections.html:
Only if you do work before closing. Vancouver requires a residential building permit for building, altering, adding to, repairing or demolishing homes. Typical permitted projects:

  • Additions and remodels
  • Adding a garage, carport, deck or patio cover
  • Adding or removing walls
  • Converting a basement, attic or garage into living space
  • Changing the footprint of a structure

Small stand-alone electrical, mechanical or plumbing jobs fall under a trade permit instead, and tree removal needs a city permit. Suspect an earlier owner skipped a permit? A field evaluation permit lets city inspectors decide which permits and corrections are needed. Call the Permit Center at 360-487-7833.

The city's updated zoning code allows more middle housing, up to six units on one lot. A buyer with development plans may value a lot differently than someone who just wants to move in.

Landlords selling inside city limits should know about two programs. Since January 1, 2026, owners of residential rentals in Vancouver register each unit every year for $30 per unit. Health and safety inspections are planned to begin in mid 2027.

When a registered rental sells, the registration moves to the new owner within 60 days of the property transfer, with no extra fee. If you stop renting, you can deregister the property. Questions go to rentalregistration@cityofvancouver.us or 360-487-7928.

A short-term rental, meaning stays under 30 consecutive nights, carries its own permit. Applicants need a Washington business license with the city endorsement, liability coverage of at least $1 million and a mailed notice to abutting neighbors. The city caps permits at 870, which is about 1 percent of its homes. Leases and homeowners association rules still apply, so a buyer with this plan should verify the status on the city's short-term rental page.

sections.h2: Deed and excise tax in Clark County
sections.html:
In Clark County the Treasurer sees a sale before the Auditor does. The Treasurer takes the real estate excise tax, and under RCW 82.45.090 the Auditor cannot record a deed until the tax is paid or marked not due.

Payment is due 30 days after the sale date, plus a $5 processing fee. The state portion rises with price:

  • 1.10 percent on a price up to $525,000
  • 1.28 percent from $525,000.01 to $1,525,000
  • 2.75 percent from $1,525,000.01 to $3,025,000
  • 3.00 percent above $3,025,000

A local rate goes on top, and your closing agent or the Treasurer can quote the total for your price. Visit the Treasurer at 1300 Franklin Street, 2nd Floor, Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Once the tax is paid, the Auditor's Recording Department in the same building records the deed. Its number is 564-397-2208.

The form in RCW 64.06.020 applies to improved residential property. Sellers deliver it within five business days of a mutually accepted written contract unless the parties choose a different schedule, and the buyer can then rescind within three business days.

Known unpermitted work goes on the form. Selling as-is does not erase that duty, although it does mean you are not promising repairs.

With no lender, a cash buyer needs no appraisal or loan approval, so the house does not have to meet a bank's condition rules. The county steps stay the same: disclosure form, excise tax at the Treasurer and recording at the Auditor. Title or escrow staff usually walk the papers through both offices.

Before you accept, estimate your net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, find out who pays the excise tax and get the closing date written down. With a rental, ask how the buyer plans to handle the tenant and the registration transfer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Vancouver, WA house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, and they are common. The disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 still applies, and unpermitted work you know about belongs on it.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when a Vancouver house sells?
faqs.a: The Clark County Auditor's Recording Department, but only after the Treasurer handles the excise tax affidavit. Both offices are at 1300 Franklin Street, and title or escrow companies normally submit the paperwork for you.

faqs.q: What happens to my Vancouver rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The new owner takes it over within 60 days of the transfer at no added fee. If the buyer will live there, the registration can instead be ended by deregistering.

faqs.q: Does Vancouver cap short-term rental permits?
faqs.a: Yes, at 870 permits, roughly 1 percent of homes. A buyer counting on short-term rental income should ask the Permit Center about availability before paying extra.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Vancouver house in?
faqs.a: Most of west Vancouver is in Vancouver Public Schools and most of east Vancouver is in Evergreen Public Schools. Small portions are in the Camas and Battle Ground districts, so check the address with the district.
